title: LOUISVILLE VILLAGE BOARD MEETS
full_story:
The Louisville Village Board met Thursday evening and worked through a light agenda in short order.

Mayor Chris Rinehart called the meeting to order. With no visitors present, he bypassed public comment and moved to approve the meeting agenda, past meeting minutes and the bills. Trustees quickly approved those items.

The mayor asked the board to approve an ordinance that corrected the makeup of the recently approved TIF 2 District. Rinehart said the county pointed out that two parcels of the new TIF district also lay in the TIF 1 District, a situation that cannot stand. The ordinance removes the parcels from TIF 1 while keeping them in TIF 2. The board approved the ordinance without dissent.

The village plans to continue the annual practice of updating sidewalks and has budgeted $30,000 for the effort. Utilities Superintendent Troy Elwood said the village would like to seek bids to determine how many linear feet it can complete for that amount. Discussion focused on sidewalk width—four or five feet—and the need to install and properly backfill the sidewalks so they sit level with the surrounding grade, free of dirt clumps, with grass seed planted. As members debated the logic of using five-foot widths in some areas and four-foot widths in others, they decided bidders should quote both options so the village can choose how best to spend the allocated money. Members approved a motion to that effect 5-0 (Trustee Scott Ikemire was absent).

Mayor Rinehart asked members to approve sending three people to the Illinois Municipal League Annual Conference in Chicago on September 17-19. Members approved the measure with no objection.

The meeting then turned to security cameras. The village already owns four cameras purchased through its vendor, Security Alarm of Salem. Mayor Rinehart suggested buying two more cameras and adding the ability to monitor all of them from the village hall. Trustees noted that Security Alarm cannot add cameras in the configuration the village wants. Rinehart recommended switching to Wabash Communications, which can set up the system as desired. After discussion, trustees approved a motion to accept Wabash Communications’ offer, which includes a one-time $750 installation fee and a monthly fee of $69, and to end the agreement with Security Alarm. The motion passed without dissent.

Next, the board discussed replacing the air conditioning system at the village hall. Rinehart said the old system is aging and he would like to replace it. He noted the project is in the budget. Trustees Craig Clifton and Chuck Smith asked whether the system has experienced problems and the answer was no. Rinehart preferred to act before it fails. Clifton and Smith felt the village should wait until a problem arises. With no consensus, the board tabled the issue until a future meeting.

Another budgeted item is a new truck for the Utility Department. Superintendent Elwood said the department has obtained quotes from a local GMC dealer and Chevrolet; it will also consider a Dodge Ram pickup. Elwood expects the truck to cost between $53,000 and $57,000. Members approved seeking quotes from various sources with a cost not to exceed $60,000.

With the agenda items complete, the meeting moved to open time, when trustees share various ideas. The wide-ranging discussion included Trustee Tim Davis’ proposal from the last meeting to install tornado warning sirens. Mayor Rinehart said he is waiting for a callback on that project.

Rinehart also addressed plans to install new Welcome to Louisville signage at the four entrances to town. He said he had talked with Matt Bible about placing a sign farther out on Kinmundy Road on Bible’s property, and he was open to the idea. At the previous meeting, someone suggested installing remotely controlled magnetic locks on the doors at the Pavilion. While the board took no action, the remotely lockable doors feature might be included in the camera purchase trustees discussed earlier.  Trustees also suggested staining the wooden posts of the pavilion but took no action. They discussed the condition of the Genealogical Building and possible improvements.

Near the end of the meeting, members considered painting murals on the sides of certain downtown buildings; some trustees appeared to be receptive to the idea.

The final item was not an action item, but the board reached consensus on setting Trick-or-Treat Night in Louisville. Setting the date is part of the mayor’s duties. Mayor Rinehart announced that Trick-or-Treat Night will be Wednesday, October 28, ahead of Fall Festival on October 29, 30 and 31. He added that local churches held their trunk-or-treat event on the courthouse square last year, to great success and they plan to do so again this year too.  With all business complete, the meeting adjourned.

title: PUBLIC INFORMATION MEETING
full_story:
The City of Flora will have a public information meeting on Monday at 4:15 pm.  The city is pursuing funding through the Illinois Transportation Enhancement Program (ITEP) for proposed sidewalk improvements to create safer pedestrian routes to local schools and the industrial park.

Residents, parents, property owners, employees, and community members are encouraged to attend, learn about the proposed project, ask questions, and share input.

The city needs the community to show their support for the project.  The meeting will be at 4:15 pm on Monday at Flora City Hall.

title: WAYNE COUNTY ARRESTS
full_story:
Wayne County Sheriff’s deputies arrested three suspects Wednesday night following a brief chase.  Sheriff Chris Otey reports that deputies attempted to stop a vehicle in Rinard at about 9 pm.

The vehicle fled to a driveway and the male driver fled on foot and the passenger Stacy L. Highsmith was detained.  Clay County K9 assisted deputies and began calling out subjects inside a residence.  Timothy W. Highsmith exited the residence and was detained for a valid Clay County Warrant.  Later Don C. Raley the driver of the vehicle, surrendered and exited the residence and was taken into custody.

A subsequent search of the vehicle showed the passenger Stacy Highsmith was in possession of methamphetamine.  All three subjects were taken into custody.

Don C. Raley, 62, of Rinard, faces charges of Fleeing or attempting to elude, Driving on Revoked License, Obstructing justice and a Clay County Warrant.  Stacy L. Highsmith, 51, of Rinard, faces charges of Possession of Methamphetamine, and Timothy W. Highsmith was taken into custody on a Clay County Warrant.

title: INGRAHAM LABOR DAY PICNIC
full_story:
The Annual Ingraham Labor Day Picnic & Tractor Pull is Monday, September 7th.

With an entry fee of $20.00, the truck pull begins at 9:00 am, followed by the modified, stock, diesel and tractor pulls at 1:00 pm, including the Illinois Stock Pullers Association, the Central Illinois Tractor Pullers Association, and the Illinois Hot Farm Stock Pullers, plus Stock Farm Class and Brush Class Semi Trucks, with the gate admission at $10.00 for adults and $5.00 for children age 6 to 12.

The fish dinner will cost $10.00 per person, and will be prepared and served by the Ingraham Firemen, with serving from 11:00 to 2:00, then vegetable soup will be available at 4:00 pm, either by the bowl at $3.00 each or by bulk sale after 5:00 at $20.00 a gallon, bring your own container.

There will also be a novelty stand, ice cream, treasured baskets, a 50/50 raffle, and more.

To reserve booth space contact Tammy Prochazka at 618-843-9648 and for more information on the truck and tractor pull call Dusty Thompson at 618-676-2304.

title: ILLINOIS STATE FAIR GEAR
full_story:
Fairgoers have a new way to take home a piece of the Illinois State Fair this year with the addition of a new official merchandise stand on the fairgrounds.

Located on Illinois Avenue across from the Sky Glide, the merchandise stand will be open throughout the fair, offering visitors the opportunity to shop for exclusive Illinois State Fair apparel as well as merchandise from that evening’s Grandstand concert.

The merchandise stand will be open each day of the fair from 10 am to 11 pm.

The first collection of Illinois State Fair merchandise features four adult T-shirts, one adult sweatshirt, and two youth T-shirts, with prices ranging from $35 to $80.

The collection celebrates some of the Illinois State Fair’s most beloved traditions including the butter cow, horse racing and the iconic corn dog.  Whether you’re looking for a keepsake from your day at the fair or official gear from your favorite Grandstand artist, the new merchandise stand offers something for every fair fan.

As a reminder, tickets are on sale for all Grandstand shows and auto races on ticketmaster.com and in-person at the Illinois State Fair Grandstand Box Office.  Tonight’s Grandstand concert will be by former Louisville resident Bailey Zimmerman.

Stay up to date with all the latest news and announcements from the Illinois State Fair by connecting to their Facebook, Twitter and Instagram accounts.

title: ROBBINS PLEADS NOT GUILTY
full_story:
Stacey R. Robbins, 47, of rural Fairfield waived formal arraignment Tuesday afternoon in Wayne County Circuit Court and entered a not guilty plea to charges she faked a cancer diagnosis to scam money from sympathetic donors.

Robbins is charged with theft, a Class-2 felony and deceptive practice, a Class-4 felony.  Circuit Judge Denton Aud set the case for a pretrial hearing on September 8th.

In the theft case, the State alleges that Robbins collected cash from a number of individual donors and through various school fundraisers and various fundraisers at the Roads Church near Norris City.  In the deceptive practice case, Robbins is accused of taking more than $7,000 from a GoFundMe page that a friend set up.

title: MEMORIAL DEDICATION
full_story:
State Representative Blaine Wilhour provided remarks Tuesday at a ceremony honoring two local servicemen who were killed in the line of duty in Afghanistan.  Chief Warrant Officer 2 Christopher Donaldson and Sergeant Timothy Sayne were killed in 2006 and 2011, respectively.

“Thank you to the Donaldson and Sayne families and Commissioner Libby Moeller for their persistence and dedication to honor these two local heroes,” commented Wilhour.  “It was impressive to see over 200 family, friends, and veterans in attendance for these two men who loved America and made the ultimate sacrifice for all of us.”

The 4th Street overpass was dedicated as the Chief Warrant Officer 2 Christopher Donaldson Memorial Overpass and the Fayette Avenue overpass was dedicated as the Sergeant Timothy Sayne Memorial Overpass.  In addition to Wilhour, the program included comments by Representative Adam Niemerg, Senator Steve McClure, Mayor Mike Schutzbach, and Commissioner Libby Moeller at the public ceremony held outside the Workman Sports Complex in Effingham.

The ceremony included a presentation of colors by Effingham American Legion Post 120.  Evie Sayne sang the National Anthem, while Page Brummer, Aliyah Bunton, Shae Conder, Rowyn Frey, Henry Gannaway, Max Gillenwater, and Evie Sayne performed “God Bless America.”  Reverend Mike Burdick of St. John’s Lutheran Church provided the benediction, followed by a moment of silence in honor of Sayne and Donaldson.

title: SALES TAX HOLIDAY
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Revenue’s State Sales Tax Holiday for certain clothing and school-related items ends Sunday.

The state sales tax holiday started on Friday, August 7th.  During the Sales Tax Holiday consumers can purchase certain clothing and school-related items and pay sales tax at a reduced rate.  The state’s portion of sales tax due throughout the holiday is reduced by 5% from 6.25% to 1.25%.  Items include traditional supplies such as markers and pencils, notebooks and folders and other classroom items, as well as many clothing purchases.  Clothing items, including shoes, that cost less than $125 will qualify for a lower sales tax rate, while there will be no price limit on school supplies.

The last time the state approved such a program was in 2022, the last time JB Pritzker ran for reelection.

title: LIBRARY LITERACY GRANTS
full_story:
Illinois Secretary of State and State Librarian Alexi Giannoulias awarded a combined $28.9 million in grants to support library services and literacy programs throughout Illinois.

The grants include awards to regional library systems to enhance online catalogs at local libraries, support day-to-day operations and expand interlibrary loan programs.  Funding also supports radio information services that provide local news and information to individuals who cannot read standard print materials.  Literacy grants promote basic reading, math, writing and English language skills through adult, family and workplace literacy programs.

“Libraries are cornerstones of our communities, providing Illinoisans with access to information, technology, educational resources and opportunities to learn and grow,” Giannoulias said.  “These grants strengthen our libraries and literacy programs and help protect the fundamental Right to Read, ensuring people of all ages and abilities can access the information and resources they need to succeed.”

The nearly $6.8 million in literacy grants will fund 104 programs serving adults and families throughout Illinois.  Receiving grants locally are Frontier Community College Adult Literacy in Fairfield will get $81,500.  And C.E.F.S. in Effingham will get $80,300 for Adult Literacy.

The grants are funded through a combination of state and federal resources, including funding appropriated by the Illinois General Assembly and federal Library Services and Technology Act funding administered through the Institute of Museum and Library Services.

As part of Illinois’ commitment to protecting the Right to Read, library recipients also are required to adopt the American Library Association’s Library Bill of Rights or a similar policy prohibiting the banning or removal of library materials based on partisan or doctrinal disapproval.

While libraries in other states have faced efforts to reduce funding, cut hours and services, and restrict access to books and other materials, Illinois is taking a different approach.  Since taking office Secretary Giannoulias’ administration have awarded more than $214 million in grants to strengthen libraries, expand literacy programs and ensure Illinoisans have the resources they need to learn, grow and exercise their fundamental Right to Read.
